dataset.name: Amazon EU FBA Fee Rates 2026 (Pan-EU & EFN)
dataset.description: Amazon European marketplace FBA fee schedule for 2026: full official fulfilment fee tables by store and size class (13 classes: envelopes, parcels and bulky tiers, weight rows as published), referral rates by category, Pan-EU storage countries, EFN cross-border surcharges, per-kg overage rates, the verified monthly storage table (UK in £ per cubic foot, EU in € and SE in SEK per cubic metre), the 1.5% fuel & logistics surcharge (rising to 2% from 2026-11-02, official), and the 2026 EU cross-border import charges — a €3.00 per item statutory customs duty (Regulation (EU) 2026/382, effective 2026-07-01) plus the Union handling fee of €2.00 per item (delegated regulation C(2026) 6694 adopted 2026-09-21, effective 2026-11-01, applying to distance sales above EUR 150 as well as below). Both are declared and paid by the declarant — in practice the platform or the non-EU seller — and Amazon passes them on in the customer-facing price at checkout, so they are not deducted from seller net profit. Fulfilment tables transcribed programmatically from Amazon's official xlsx rate tables (Seller Central exports, originals archived 2026-10-23); storage checked against the official monthly storage card; import charges checked against EUR-Lex and European Commission primary sources.

sources.name: Amazon Seller Central EU fee pages (UK/DE/FR/IT/ES/NL/PL/SE), Jan 2026 rate card
Amazon Seller Central — Monthly storage fees (UK store rate card, effective 2026-02-01; verified 2026-09-15)
Amazon UK pricing page — FBA storage fees and the 1.5% fuel & logistics surcharge (effective 2026-04-17; verified 2026-09-15)

dataset.how_to_cite: ylishi.tools, Amazon EU FBA fee rates 2026 (DE/FR/IT/ES/NL/PL/SE/UK), https://ylishi.tools/rates/fba-eu-2026.json, CC BY 4.0
dataset.note: EU 2026 change: Amazon CUT fulfillment fees (UK -£0.26, DE -€0.32 typical) and slashed low-price apparel referral (≤€15: 8%→5%, €15-20: 15%→10%) — opposite of the US 3.5% fuel surcharge. Jan-5 batch: Home 15%→8% ≤€20 (new cat), Pet Clothing & Food 15%→5% ≤€10, Grocery & Gourmet and Vitamins/Minerals/Supplements 8%→5% ≤€10 (new cat), Low-price FBA extended to ≤€20.

_meta.de_note: DE uses the CE (Mitteleuropa: DE/PL/CZ) column; the DE-only column differs by +0.26 EUR cross-border add-on per footnote 4.
_meta.unit_note: PL rows are in PLN, SE in SEK, UK in GBP, all others EUR; storage for PL is EUR (see monthly_storage).

referral_bands_2026.note: Standard rates above; official 2026 banded reductions (RR stays the headline rate).

effective.date_conflict_note: The EN aboutamazon letter dates the fulfilment+clothing tranche 2025-12-15 (and the home/pet/grocery/lp-FBA tranche 2026-01-05), while the PL letter dates its listed changes 2026-02-01; the official xlsx footnote says parcel rows 2025-12-15 and ALL other changes 2026-02-01. Operative date for non-parcel items = 2026-02-01 (current official card).

fuel_surcharge_scheduled.note: Official: from 2 November 2026 the fuel and logistics-related surcharge increases from 1.5% to 2% on FBA fulfilment fees in these stores. Peak fees 15 Oct 2026 - 14 Jan 2027 (DE/UK selected orders) also carry the surcharge.

rates.fuel_surcharge_note: CONFIRMED against official Seller Central (checked 2026-10-23; supersedes the earlier media-only PENDING note). 1.5% applied to fulfilment fees in the UK, France, Germany, Italy, Spain, Poland, Sweden, Netherlands, Ireland and Belgium stores from 17 April 2026. This is NOT the US rate — the US applies 3.5%. Do not reuse one market's surcharge for the other.

eu_import_charges.scope: shipments sent from outside the EU to consumers in the EU. Orders fulfilled from stock already inside the EU, and inbound replenishments into an Amazon EU fulfilment centre, are not subject to these charges.

statutory_duty.basis: per item / tariff line declared on the customs entry
statutory_duty.kind: EU law, not an Amazon fee
statutory_duty.transitional: flat rate until the EU customs data hub is operational (expected 2028); normal tariff rates apply afterwards
statutory_duty.threshold_note: applies to consignments with an inherent value of EUR 150 or less

amazon_customs_handling.basis: per item on cross-border FBA shipments
amazon_customs_handling.display: added to the customer-facing price at checkout, alongside the statutory duty
amazon_customs_handling.legal_instrument: European Commission delegated regulation C(2026) 6694, adopted 2026-09-21
amazon_customs_handling.kind: EU Union handling fee (customs processing), not an Amazon fee and not a duty
amazon_customs_handling.payer: declarant — in practice the platform or the non-EU seller, not the buyer
amazon_customs_handling.threshold_note: unlike the EUR 3 duty, applies to consignments above EUR 150 as well as below
amazon_customs_handling.unit_note: national authorities read 'item' as either each product or each tariff line; model both readings on multi-product orders

eu_import_charges.who_pays_legal: declarant (platform / non-EU seller) — Amazon then passes the charge through to the buyer at checkout
eu_import_charges.seller_impact: Not deducted from seller net profit — Amazon adds both charges on top of the price you set, so the buyer pays EUR 5.00 more per item. The real effect is competitive: against an EU-local seller the customer sees your offer EUR 5.00 dearer. Amazon asks sellers to compare their shelf price (set price + import duty + duty VAT) with locally fulfilled listings and to re-check pricing rules.
eu_import_charges.vat_note: destination-country import VAT applies in addition to the duty (DE 19%, FR 20%, IT 22%)
exemptions: orders fulfilled from stock inside the EU
inbound replenishments to an Amazon EU fulfilment centre
the UK marketplace (the UK is not an EU customs territory)
goods above EUR 150 are outside the EUR 3 flat duty, but the EUR 2 handling fee still applies to them

official_sources.name: EUR-Lex OJ: Council Regulation (EU) 2026/382 (EUR 3 duty, 1 Jul 2026 - 1 Jul 2028)
European Commission: EU Customs Reform (EUR 2 Union handling fee from 1 Nov 2026)

monthly_storage.unit_note: UK is billed per cubic FOOT per month; every other European store is billed per cubic METRE per month. The two are not comparable without converting, and cross-market values get copied with nothing changed but the currency symbol.

storage_utilisation_surcharge_uk_per_cuf.base_definition: the standard column is the 'all other categories' standard rate (0.76 Jan-Sep / 1.51 Oct-Dec); the oversize column is the oversize rate (0.55 / 0.87)
storage_utilisation_surcharge_uk_per_cuf.note: The surcharge is charged ON TOP of the base monthly storage fee and only on inventory aged over 30 days. The surcharge column itself does not change between Jan-Sep and Oct-Dec — only the base rate does.

verbatim_rows: UK (based on cubic feet per month) £0.62 £0.82 £0.76 £1.51 £0.55 £0.87
Germany, France, Italy, Spain, Belgium, the Netherlands and Poland (based on cubic metres per month) €19.99 €29.23 €27.54 €52.20 €21.78 €34.49

_meta.units: UK = GBP per cubic foot; EU (‘欧盟’ group as published) = EUR per cubic metre; rates rounded to 2dp
_meta.category_exclusion: The 241-270 band excludes clothing & accessories, shoes, backpacks & handbags, luggage, jewellery and watches; other bands apply to all goods.
_meta.charged_in_addition_to: monthly storage fee (not instead of it)

rates.efn_cross_border_surcharge_per_unit_note: Semantics: this field is the official footnote-4 cross-border add-on for German stock outside the Central Europe programme (per destination store: 0.26 EUR / 0.26 GBP / 2.50 SEK / 1.15 PLN). It is NOT the European Fulfilment Network fee — EFN is a separate official per-unit table that replaces the local fee (see https://ylishi.tools/tools/efn-fees/).

worked_example.note: DE standard parcel <=1.90kg (CE column, official xlsx), price €29.99: fulfillment 3.69 + referral max(29.99x0.15,0.3)=4.50
